senses.en: extremely important; absolutely necessary
an essential or urgent thing
(grammar) expressing a command

ex.en: It is imperative that you finish the application before Friday.
ex.zh: 你必須在星期五前完成申請，這非常重要。

root.note: 如命令般必須做的 → 必要的

senses.en: so slight or gradual that it cannot be noticed

ex.en: The change in the room's temperature was almost imperceptible.
ex.zh: 房間溫度的變化幾乎察覺不到。

root.note: 無法感知到的 → 察覺不到的

senses.en: not capable of being made perfect

ex.en: The philosopher argued that human nature is imperfectible.
ex.zh: 那位哲學家主張人性無法臻於完美。

root.note: 不能被做到完美的

senses.en: to put something or someone in danger

ex.en: Cutting the safety budget could imperil the lives of workers.
ex.zh: 削減安全預算可能會危及工人的生命。

root.note: 使進入危險 → 危及

senses.en: arrogant and domineering; expecting to be obeyed

ex.en: With an imperious wave of her hand, she dismissed the servants.
ex.zh: 她傲慢地揮揮手，把僕人打發走。

root.note: 總在發號施令的 → 專橫的

senses.en: not allowed

ex.en: Using a phone during the exam is impermissible.
ex.zh: 考試時使用手機是不被允許的。

root.note: 不能放行的 → 不容許的

senses.en: not showing personal feelings or warmth
not relating to any particular person

ex.en: The hospital felt cold and impersonal to the frightened child.
ex.zh: 對那個害怕的孩子來說，醫院感覺冰冷又沒有人情味。

root.note: 不帶個人情感的

senses.en: to pretend to be another person, for fun or to deceive

ex.en: It is a crime to impersonate a police officer.
ex.zh: 冒充警察是犯罪行為。

root.note: 進入別人的角色 → 冒充

senses.en: impossible to persuade

ex.en: My grandmother was impersuadable once she had made up her mind.
ex.zh: 我奶奶一旦下定決心，就誰也說服不了。

root.note: 勸不動的

senses.en: rude lack of respect

ex.en: The teacher would not tolerate such impertinence from a student.
ex.zh: 老師無法容忍學生如此無禮。

root.note: 不得體、不恰當 → 無禮

senses.en: unable to be upset; always calm

ex.en: The pilot remained imperturbable even during the violent storm.
ex.zh: 即使在猛烈的暴風雨中，機長依然泰然自若。

root.note: 無法被擾亂的 → 冷靜的

senses.en: not allowing liquid or gas to pass through
not affected or influenced by something
senses.zh: 不受影響的；無動於衷的

ex.en: He seemed impervious to criticism and kept doing things his own way.
ex.zh: 他似乎對批評無動於衷，照樣我行我素。

root.note: 沒有路可通過的 → 不透的；不受影響的

senses.en: the quality of acting quickly without thinking

ex.en: His youthful impetuosity led him to quit his job without a plan.
ex.zh: 年輕人的衝動讓他沒有任何計畫就辭職了。

root.note: 猛衝向前的性格 → 衝動

senses.en: something that encourages a process or activity to happen
(physics) the force that makes an object move

ex.en: The new funding gave fresh impetus to the research project.
ex.zh: 新的經費為研究計畫注入新的動力。

root.note: 向前衝的力量 → 推動力

senses.en: lack of respect for God or religion

ex.en: In ancient Athens, Socrates was accused of impiety.
ex.zh: 在古雅典，蘇格拉底被控不敬神。

root.note: 不虔誠

senses.en: showing a lack of respect for God or religion

ex.en: The villagers considered it impious to work on holy days.
ex.zh: 村民們認為在聖日工作是不敬神的。

root.note: 不虔誠的

mn: 注意重音在第一音節：IM-pious，和 pious 不一樣。

senses.en: not seeming reasonable or likely to be true
senses.zh: 難以置信的；不合情理的

ex.en: His excuse that a dog ate his homework sounded implausible.
ex.zh: 他說作業被狗吃掉，這個藉口聽起來很難讓人相信。

root.note: 不值得讚許、不可信的

senses.en: not bending easily; inflexible

ex.en: The old leather had become dry and impliable.
ex.zh: 那塊舊皮革已經變得又乾又硬。

root.note: 不能彎折的 → 不柔順的

senses.en: to show that someone is involved in a crime or wrongdoing
to suggest as a cause

ex.en: New evidence may implicate the manager in the fraud.
ex.zh: 新證據可能顯示經理涉入這起詐欺案。

root.note: 被折進去 → 牽連

senses.en: suggested but not directly stated
complete and without doubt

ex.en: There was an implicit threat in his polite words.
ex.zh: 他客氣的話語中暗藏威脅。

root.note: 折在裡面、沒攤開說 → 含蓄的

senses.en: to suggest something without saying it directly

ex.en: Are you trying to imply that I was lying?
ex.zh: 你是在暗示我說謊嗎？

root.note: 把意思折在話裡 → 暗示

mn: 說話的人 imply（暗示），聽話的人 infer（推論）。

senses.en: unwise; likely to cause problems

ex.en: It would be impolitic to criticize the boss at the company party.
ex.zh: 在公司聚會上批評老闆是不明智的。

root.note: 不精明的 → 失策的

senses.en: the act of bringing goods into a country from abroad

ex.en: The government banned the importation of certain plants to protect local crops.
ex.zh: 政府禁止進口某些植物，以保護本地作物。

root.note: 運進來 → 進口

senses.en: annoyingly persistent in asking for something

ex.en: The importunate salesman called my office five times in one day.
ex.zh: 那個糾纏不休的推銷員一天打了五次電話到我辦公室。

root.note: 不合時宜、令人不便的 → 糾纏不休的

senses.en: to ask someone repeatedly and annoyingly for something

ex.en: Street vendors importune tourists to buy their souvenirs.
ex.zh: 街頭小販不停糾纏遊客買紀念品。

root.note: 在不方便的時候煩人 → 糾纏

senses.en: unable to take effective action; powerless
(of a man) unable to achieve an erection

ex.en: The small country felt impotent against its powerful neighbor.
ex.zh: 這個小國面對強大的鄰國感到無能為力。

root.note: 沒有力量的 → 無力的

senses.en: to make someone poor
to make something weaker or worse in quality

ex.en: Years of war can impoverish even a wealthy nation.
ex.zh: 多年戰爭即使是富國也會變窮。

root.note: 使陷入貧窮

senses.en: impossible to do or carry out in practice

ex.en: The plan to move the whole village was impracticable.
ex.zh: 把整個村莊遷走的計畫根本行不通。

root.note: 無法實行的

mn: impracticable（做不到）比 impractical（不實際、不切實用）更強烈。

senses.en: unable to be captured or broken into
unable to be defeated or challenged

ex.en: The castle on the cliff was nearly impregnable.
ex.zh: 懸崖上的城堡幾乎堅不可摧。

parts.m: take, seize 奪取（拉丁文 prehendere）

root.note: 無法被奪取的 → 攻不破的

senses.en: to soak or fill something with a substance
to make pregnant

ex.en: Workers impregnate the wood with chemicals to prevent rot.
ex.zh: 工人把木材浸透化學藥劑以防腐爛。

root.note: 使懷有 → 使充滿

senses.en: done without planning or preparation
without preparation

ex.en: The band gave an impromptu performance in the train station.
ex.zh: 樂團在火車站即興演出。

root.note: 「在手邊就緒」→ 立即、即興的

senses.en: not suitable or appropriate
not following rules or law

ex.en: Improper storage can cause food to spoil quickly.
ex.zh: 保存方式不當會讓食物很快壞掉。

root.note: 不適當的

senses.en: improper or unacceptable behavior

ex.en: The senator denied any impropriety in accepting the gift.
ex.zh: 那位參議員否認收受禮物有任何不當之處。

root.note: 不適當 → 不當行為

senses.en: not planning or saving for the future

ex.en: His improvident spending left him with no savings for retirement.
ex.zh: 他花錢不顧將來，結果退休時一點積蓄都沒有。

root.note: 不往前看的 → 不顧將來的

senses.en: to create or perform something without preparation
to make something from whatever is available

ex.en: When the power went out, we had to improvise with candles.
ex.zh: 停電時，我們只好拿蠟燭湊合著用。

root.note: 事先沒看過、沒準備 → 即興

senses.en: not showing care for the consequences; unwise

ex.en: It would be imprudent to invest all your savings in one company.
ex.zh: 把所有積蓄投資在一家公司是不明智的。

root.note: 沒有遠見的 → 輕率的

senses.en: rude and disrespectful behavior

ex.en: She had the impudence to laugh at the principal's warning.
ex.zh: 她竟然厚著臉皮嘲笑校長的警告。

root.note: 不知羞恥 → 厚顏無恥

senses.en: to question or attack the truth, honesty, or validity of something

ex.en: The lawyer tried to impugn the witness's credibility.
ex.zh: 律師試圖質疑證人的可信度。

root.note: 對著打 → 抨擊、質疑

mn: 字根 pugn（打鬥）也出現在 pugnacious（好鬥的）；g 不發音。

senses.en: a strong urge to do something
the force that pushes something forward

ex.en: She felt a sudden impulsion to call her old friend.
ex.zh: 她突然有股衝動想打電話給老朋友。

root.note: 往前推 → 推動；衝動

senses.en: acting suddenly without thinking carefully

ex.en: He regretted his impulsive decision to buy the expensive phone.
ex.zh: 他後悔自己一時衝動買了那支昂貴的手機。

root.note: 被一股力量推著走的 → 衝動的

senses.en: freedom from punishment or harmful consequences

ex.en: The gang operated with impunity because the police were bribed.
ex.zh: 因為警察被收買，那個幫派為所欲為而不受懲罰。

root.note: 不被懲罰

mn: 常見片語 with impunity：肆無忌憚地、不受懲罰地。

senses.en: mixed with other substances; not pure
morally wrong

ex.en: The gold was impure and contained traces of copper.
ex.zh: 這塊金子不純，含有少量的銅。

root.note: 不純的

senses.en: to attribute a fault or quality to someone

ex.en: It is unfair to impute bad motives to people you do not know.
ex.zh: 把不良動機歸咎於你不認識的人是不公平的。

root.note: 把（責任）算到某人身上 → 歸咎

senses.en: impossible or very difficult to reach
difficult to understand or use
senses.zh: 難以理解的；難以取得的

ex.en: The village is inaccessible by car during the rainy season.
ex.zh: 雨季時汽車無法開到那個村莊。

root.note: 無法走到的 → 難以到達的

senses.en: not correct or exact

ex.en: The map was inaccurate, so we got lost twice.
ex.zh: 地圖不準確，害我們迷路了兩次。

root.note: 不精確的

senses.en: not active or working

ex.en: The volcano has been inactive for thousands of years.
ex.zh: 這座火山已經數千年沒有活動了。

root.note: 不動的

senses.en: not enough or not good enough
(of a person) unable to deal with a situation
senses.zh: （人）能力不足的；自覺不夠好的

ex.en: The hospital's supply of beds was inadequate for the flu season.
ex.zh: 醫院的病床數量不足以應付流感季節。

root.note: 達不到相等（所需）的程度 → 不足的

senses.en: not allowed, especially as evidence in court
senses.zh: （法庭上）不予採納的；不容許的

ex.en: The judge ruled that the illegally recorded call was inadmissible.
ex.zh: 法官裁定那通非法錄音的電話不能作為證據。

root.note: 不能被放進來的 → 不予採納的

senses.en: not done on purpose; accidental

ex.en: An inadvertent click sent the email to the wrong person.
ex.zh: 不小心點了一下，郵件就寄錯人了。

root.note: 沒把注意力轉過去的 → 無意的

senses.en: likely to have bad results; unwise

ex.en: Doctors say it is inadvisable to swim right after a large meal.
ex.zh: 醫生說飽餐後馬上游泳是不明智的。

root.note: 不值得建議的 → 不明智的

senses.en: silly and without meaning

ex.en: I got tired of their inane chatter about celebrity gossip.
ex.zh: 我受夠了他們聊名人八卦的無聊廢話。

root.note: 空洞的 → 無意義的

senses.en: not alive

ex.en: Young children often talk to inanimate objects like toys.
ex.zh: 小孩子常常跟玩具之類無生命的東西說話。

root.note: 沒有生命的

senses.en: impossible to understand or grasp

ex.en: To the child, the lecture on quantum physics was inapprehensible.
ex.zh: 對那個孩子來說，量子物理的演講完全無法理解。

root.note: 無法抓住（意思）的 → 不可理解的

senses.en: not suitable or appropriate

ex.en: Comparing the tragedy to a sports game was an inapt remark.
ex.zh: 把這場悲劇比作一場球賽是很不恰當的說法。

root.note: 不適合的

mn: inapt 是「不恰當」；inept 是「笨拙無能」。

senses.en: unable to express ideas clearly
senses.zh: 口齒不清的；不善表達的

senses.en: not expressed in words

ex.en: He was so nervous that he became inarticulate during the interview.
ex.zh: 他緊張到面試時話都說不清楚。

root.note: 無法清楚分節發音的 → 口齒不清的

senses.en: impossible to hear

ex.en: Her voice was almost inaudible over the noise of the traffic.
ex.zh: 在車流噪音中，她的聲音幾乎聽不見。

root.note: 聽不到的

senses.en: existing from birth; natural

ex.en: Some scientists believe that the ability to learn language is inborn.
ex.zh: 有些科學家認為學習語言的能力是與生俱來的。

root.note: 出生時就在身上的 → 天生的

senses.en: produced by breeding closely related individuals
existing as a deep part of one's nature

ex.en: Inbred dogs are more likely to suffer from health problems.
ex.zh: 近親繁殖的狗比較容易有健康問題。

root.note: 在同一群體內繁殖的 → 近親繁殖的

senses.en: light produced by something that is very hot

ex.en: The incandescence of the molten metal lit up the whole factory.
ex.zh: 熔融金屬發出的白熱光芒照亮了整座工廠。

root.note: 發出光熱的狀態 → 白熱

senses.en: giving off light when heated
extremely bright, passionate, or angry
senses.zh: 光彩奪目的；極度激動的

ex.en: Many cities have replaced incandescent bulbs with LED lights.
ex.zh: 許多城市已把白熾燈泡換成 LED 燈。

root.note: 熾熱發光的

senses.en: to prevent someone from functioning normally
senses.zh: 使失去能力；使無法行動

ex.en: A back injury can incapacitate a worker for weeks.
ex.zh: 背部受傷可能讓工人好幾週無法工作。

root.note: 使失去能力

senses.en: lack of ability or strength to do something

ex.en: The leader's incapacity to make decisions frustrated the entire team.
ex.zh: 領導者無法做決定，讓整個團隊很沮喪。

root.note: 沒有能力

senses.en: to put in prison

ex.en: Some reformers argue that it is costly to incarcerate nonviolent offenders.
ex.zh: 有些改革者主張監禁非暴力犯的成本太高。

root.note: 關進監獄

senses.en: designed to cause fires
tending to stir up conflict or anger

ex.en: The politician's incendiary speech sparked protests across the city.
ex.zh: 那位政客煽動性的演說引發全市抗議。

root.note: 使燃燒的 → 縱火的；煽動的

senses.en: something that motivates or encourages someone to act

ex.en: The company offers a bonus as an incentive for good performance.
ex.zh: 公司提供獎金作為表現優良的激勵。

root.note: 原指「吹奏引人前進的曲調」→ 激勵

senses.en: the beginning of an institution or activity

ex.en: She has worked for the charity since its inception in 2005.
ex.zh: 這個慈善機構自 2005 年創立起，她就一直在那裡工作。

root.note: 著手去拿 → 開始

senses.en: relating to a beginning; initial
(grammar) expressing the start of an action

ex.en: The project was still in its inceptive stage when funding ran out.
ex.zh: 計畫還在初始階段時經費就用完了。

root.note: 開始著手的 → 初期的

senses.en: continuing without stopping

ex.en: The incessant barking of the neighbor's dog kept me awake.
ex.zh: 鄰居的狗叫個不停，吵得我睡不著。

root.note: 不停止的

senses.en: little by little; gradually

ex.en: The glacier retreated inchmeal over the centuries.
ex.zh: 幾百年來，冰河一點一點地後退。

parts.m: measure, portion 份量（古英文 mǣlum）

root.note: 一英寸一英寸地 → 逐漸地

senses.en: just begun and not fully formed or developed

ex.en: Her plan for the novel was still inchoate, just a few notes and ideas.
ex.zh: 她的小說構想還沒成形，只有一些筆記和點子。

root.note: 剛開始的 → 未成形的

senses.en: (grammar) expressing the beginning of an action or state

ex.en: In English, "grow dark" has an inchoative meaning.
ex.zh: 在英文裡，「grow dark」帶有表示開始的意思。

root.note: 表示開始的

senses.en: the rate at which something happens
(physics) the way light or a ray falls on a surface

ex.en: The incidence of heart disease has fallen in recent years.
ex.zh: 近年來心臟病的發生率下降了。

root.note: 落在…上 → 發生（率）

senses.en: an event, especially an unusual or unpleasant one

ex.en: The police are investigating the incident at the train station.
ex.zh: 警方正在調查火車站發生的事件。

root.note: 落到身上的事 → 事件

senses.en: used to add information or change the subject; by the way
as a minor, unplanned result

ex.en: Incidentally, have you seen my blue umbrella anywhere?
ex.zh: 順帶一問，你有看到我的藍色雨傘嗎？

root.note: 碰巧落下的 → 附帶地

senses.en: to destroy something completely by burning

ex.en: The hospital must incinerate its medical waste safely.
ex.zh: 醫院必須安全地焚化醫療廢棄物。

root.note: 燒成灰

senses.en: the beginning or early stage of something

ex.en: Doctors caught the disease in its incipience, when treatment works best.
ex.zh: 醫生在疾病初期就發現了，這時治療效果最好。

root.note: 著手開始 → 初期

senses.en: beginning to happen or develop

ex.en: The dentist found an incipient cavity and filled it right away.
ex.zh: 牙醫發現一個初期蛀牙，立刻把它補好。

root.note: 剛著手開始的 → 初期的

senses.en: a narrow, sharp front tooth used for cutting

ex.en: The boy chipped an incisor when he fell off his bike.
ex.zh: 那個男孩騎腳踏車摔倒，撞缺了一顆門牙。

root.note: 切進去的東西 → 門牙

senses.en: to encourage or stir up violent or unlawful behavior

ex.en: He was arrested for trying to incite a riot online.
ex.zh: 他因試圖在網路上煽動暴動而被捕。

parts.m: set in motion, call 使動、召喚

root.note: 促使行動 → 煽動

senses.en: the act of encouraging violent or unlawful behavior

ex.en: The speaker was charged with incitement to violence.
ex.zh: 那位演講者被控煽動暴力。

root.note: 煽動

senses.en: impossible to force, control, or restrain
senses.zh: 無法強制的；控制不住的

ex.en: The prisoner had an incoercible will that no threat could break.
ex.zh: 那名囚犯意志堅定，任何威脅都無法使他屈服。

parts.m: shut up, restrain 關住、限制

root.note: 無法被強制的

senses.en: the quality of being unclear or lacking logical connection

ex.en: The incoherence of his essay made it hard to follow his argument.
ex.zh: 他的文章前後不連貫，讓人很難理解他的論點。

root.note: 黏不在一起 → 不連貫

senses.en: unclear and hard to understand; not logically connected

ex.en: The patient was feverish and incoherent.
ex.zh: 病人發燒而且說話語無倫次。

root.note: 黏不在一起的 → 不連貫的

senses.en: not able to burn

ex.en: The walls are lined with incombustible material to slow a fire.
ex.zh: 牆壁內襯有不可燃材料來延緩火勢。

root.note: 無法燃燒的

senses.en: so good that nothing else can be compared to it
senses.zh: 無可比擬的；無與倫比的

ex.en: The view from the summit was incomparable.
ex.zh: 從山頂看出去的景色無與倫比。

root.note: 無法比較的 → 無與倫比的

senses.en: unable to exist or work together

ex.en: This charger is incompatible with older phone models.
ex.zh: 這個充電器和舊款手機不相容。

root.note: 無法一起承受、共處的 → 不相容的

senses.en: lack of the skill or ability to do something well

ex.en: The project failed because of the manager's incompetence.
ex.zh: 這個專案因為經理的無能而失敗。

root.note: 不能勝任

senses.en: not having the skill or ability to do something well

ex.en: The customers complained about the incompetent staff at the front desk.
ex.zh: 顧客抱怨櫃台人員不稱職。

root.note: 不能勝任的

senses.en: not finished or not having all its parts

ex.en: Your application is incomplete without a photo.
ex.zh: 沒有附照片的話，你的申請就不完整。

root.note: 沒有填滿的 → 不完整的

senses.en: impossible to understand

ex.en: The instructions were written in incomprehensible technical jargon.
ex.zh: 說明書用了一堆讓人看不懂的專業術語。

root.note: 無法完全抓住（意思）的 → 無法理解的

senses.en: not able to be compressed or made smaller

ex.en: For most practical purposes, water is treated as incompressible.
ex.zh: 在大多數實際應用中，水被視為不可壓縮的。

root.note: 無法壓在一起的 → 不可壓縮的

senses.en: impossible to imagine or believe
senses.zh: 不可思議的；難以想像的

ex.en: Just a few decades ago, video calls on a phone were inconceivable.
ex.zh: 就在幾十年前，用手機視訊通話還是難以想像的事。

root.note: 腦中無法掌握的 → 難以想像的

senses.en: not in harmony with the surroundings; out of place

ex.en: The modern glass tower looks incongruous among the old temples.
ex.zh: 那棟現代玻璃大樓在古老的寺廟之間顯得格格不入。

root.note: 不一致的 → 不協調的

senses.en: not important or significant

ex.en: Don't waste time arguing over inconsequential details.
ex.zh: 別浪費時間爭論那些無關緊要的細節。

root.note: 不會帶來後果的 → 不重要的

senses.en: small in size or amount; not worth considering

ex.en: Compared with the total budget, the cost of the repairs was inconsiderable.
ex.zh: 和總預算相比，修理費用微不足道。

root.note: 不值得考慮的 → 微不足道的

mn: 常見說法 not inconsiderable：「可不少」，是英式的委婉強調。

senses.en: not staying the same in behavior or quality
not in agreement with something else

ex.en: The witness's story was inconsistent with the video evidence.
ex.zh: 證人的說法和錄影證據不相符。

root.note: 無法站在一起的 → 不一致的

senses.en: frequently changing; not faithful

ex.en: The poet complained about his inconstant lover.
ex.zh: 詩人抱怨他那善變的情人。

root.note: 站不穩的 → 善變的

senses.en: impossible to deny or dispute

ex.en: The DNA test provided incontrovertible proof of his innocence.
ex.zh: DNA 檢測提供了他清白的確鑿證據。

root.note: 無法被反轉的 → 無可爭辯的

senses.en: causing trouble or difficulty

ex.en: Is it inconvenient for you to meet on Saturday morning?
ex.zh: 星期六早上見面對你來說會不方便嗎？

root.note: 不適合一起來的 → 不方便的

senses.en: impossible to justify or excuse
senses.zh: 無法辯護的；站不住腳的

senses.en: impossible to protect against attack

ex.en: Bullying a younger student is simply indefensible.
ex.zh: 霸凌學弟妹根本沒有任何辯解的餘地。

root.note: 無法擋開攻擊的 → 無法辯護的
